regimes.name: US tax resident (citizen, green card holder or substantial presence)
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation at federal level; state income and estate taxes come on top depending on the state of residence.
regimes.eligibility: Citizens are always taxed; non-citizens are resident with a green card or under the substantial presence test (183 weighted days over 3 years, at least 31 in the current year). Non-citizens need an immigrant or long-stay visa (e.g. EB-5, E-2, L-1).

capital_gains.summary: Combined federal + South Carolina top rate on a large long-term gain: 27.2% (federal 20% + 3.8% NIIT + state 3.36%). Top rate 6% (temporarily cut from 6.2% from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026; Tax Foundation notes it is scheduled to revert to 6.2%). South Carolina deducts 44% of net long-term capital gains, so the effective rate is about 3.36% (3.47% at 6.2%). Dividends 6%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Federal: 20% bracket above USD 613,700 taxable income (MFJ, 2026); NIIT above USD 250,000 MAGI (MFJ). State: top rate reached at the thresholds stated in the summary.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: State income tax is effectively not deductible federally for a top-bracket family (SALT cap; itemized deductions limited), so state and federal rates are simply added. Most states do not give a credit for foreign taxes paid. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain on real estate is taxed federally at 25% + 3.8%.

capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains at federal and state level.

South Carolina deducts 44% of net long-term capital gains, so the effective rate is about 3.36% (3.47% at 6.2%). Dividends 6%.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No federal property tax; states and localities tax real property (and some tax personal property). A few states historically taxed intangibles.

inheritance.summary: Federal estate tax is levied on the estate at 40% on the taxable estate above the basic exclusion amount, USD 15,000,000 per person for deaths in 2026 (OBBBA made the higher exclusion permanent and indexes it from 2027). Gift and estate tax are unified: lifetime gifts above the USD 19,000 per-recipient annual exclusion use up the same USD 15 million. Unused exclusion of a deceased spouse is portable, so a married couple shelters USD 30 million. Assets get a step-up in cost basis at death, eliminating the embedded capital gain. Scored for a married couple using portability (IRC 2010(c)(2)(B), deceased spousal unused exclusion): the second estate can shelter USD 30,000,000 (2 x USD 15,000,000) if a timely Form 706 portability election is made at the first death.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per decedent (2026); annual gift exclusion USD 19,000 per donee (USD 38,000 with gift-splitting); unlimited marital deduction for a US-citizen spouse; gifts to a non-citizen spouse USD 194,000 a year (2026). GST tax exemption equals the basic exclusion.
inheritance.regional_differences: About a dozen states and DC levy estate taxes and a few levy inheritance taxes (not verified in this session; see the subnational file). Probate costs vary by state and are usually avoided with a revocable living trust.
inheritance.important_exceptions: The marital deduction for a non-citizen surviving spouse requires a qualified domestic trust (QDOT). Non-resident non-citizens: estate tax on US-situs assets (including US shares) with a filing threshold of only USD 60,000 (not indexed). Gifts or bequests received by US persons from covered expatriates are taxed to the recipient at the top rate (IRC 2801).

inheritance.spouse_note: Unlimited marital deduction for property passing to a surviving spouse (IRC 2056(a)), but only if the spouse is a US citizen or the property goes into a qualified domestic trust (2056(d)); it defers the tax, since the assets are in the survivor's estate (the unused exclusion is portable).
inheritance.gift_tax: Unified with the estate tax: 40% on lifetime gifts above the USD 19,000 annual exclusion once the USD 15 million lifetime exclusion is used; paid by the donor.
inheritance.business_relief: No exemption for business assets; IRC 6166 allows deferral of estate tax on closely held business interests over up to 14 years, and IRC 2032A special-use valuation for farms/businesses.
inheritance.foreign_assets: US citizens and US-domiciled non-citizens: worldwide estate. Non-domiciled non-citizens: US-situs assets only (US real estate, shares of US companies, tangible property in the US).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Estate tax uses domicile (living in the US with intent to remain), not the income tax residence test. Green card holders are usually domiciled. Expatriates who are covered expatriates trigger the IRC 2801 recipient tax on later gifts/bequests to US persons.

regimes.name: Irrevocable GST-exempt dynasty trust taxed as a grantor trust
regimes.description: The parents each give up to their USD 15 million gift/estate exclusion (USD 30 million for a couple) to an irrevocable trust for the children and later generations, allocating the equal GST exemption so the trust is never subject to estate or generation-skipping tax. The trust is drafted as a grantor trust (e.g. a power to swap assets), so the parents keep paying the income tax on its gains and dividends at their own rates; those payments shrink their taxable estate without counting as further gifts. Assets in the trust and all their later growth pass outside the parents' taxable estates. Federal layer only; state income and estate taxes are not reflected in this regime.
regimes.eligibility: Donors must be US citizens or US-domiciled non-citizens to use the USD 15 million exclusion (non-domiciled non-citizens have no lifetime gift exclusion). The parents must give up control and benefit: they cannot be beneficiaries (except a spouse in a spousal lifetime access trust) or hold powers that pull the assets back into their estates (IRC 2036/2038). Perpetual duration requires a trust governed by the law of a state that has abolished or extended the rule against perpetuities (e.g. South Dakota, Nevada, Delaware). Gift-splitting needs both spouses to be citizens or residents.
regimes.duration_note: No federal time limit: the GST exemption allocated when the trust is funded protects the trust permanently, and in states without a rule against perpetuities the trust can last indefinitely. Grantor-trust status ends at the grantor's death or when the power is released; the trust then pays its own income tax (see exit_and_liquidation).

structure.entity: Irrevocable dynasty trust (intentionally defective grantor trust), usually a directed trust sitused in a no-perpetuities state
structure.payout_notes: Distributions of trust capital or income to the children are not taxable to them while the trust is a grantor trust: the parents already pay the tax on all trust income (IRC 671 ff.). The parents themselves cannot receive distributions without bringing the assets back into their estates, so the family's own spending must come from assets kept outside the trust (a spousal lifetime access trust lets one spouse benefit, at the cost of using only the other spouse's exclusion). After grantor status ends, a non-grantor trust is taxed at trust rates (ordinary income at 37% above USD 16,000 and long-term gains at 20% above USD 16,250 in 2026, Rev. Proc. 2025-32, plus 3.8% NIIT) unless it distributes income, which is then taxed to the beneficiaries.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Running cost is a rough estimate (administrative or directed trustee fee, trust accounting and information returns, legal review), not sourced; investment management is assumed to stay with the family office. Grantor-trust rules: IRC 671-679 (a substitution power under IRC 675(4)(C) is the usual trigger). Estate inclusion risks: retained interests or control (IRC 2036, 2038), the reciprocal-trust doctrine for mirror-image spousal trusts, and implied agreements to benefit the grantor. The grantor's payment of the trust's income tax is not treated as a gift (Rev. Rul. 2004-64; not opened in this session). Trust assets get no step-up in basis at the grantor's death (Rev. Rul. 2023-2), so the children inherit the parents' cost basis and pay up to 23.8% when they sell, unless low-basis assets are swapped back to the grantor before death. State law matters: the trust's situs state determines perpetual duration and whether a non-grantor trust pays state income tax; Connecticut has a gift tax and some estate-tax states (e.g. New York) add back recent gifts. C-corporation alternatives are penalised: a personal holding company tax of 20% on undistributed passive income (IRC 541-542) and a 20% accumulated earnings tax (IRC 531) apply on top of 21% CIT.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Emigration of the grantor: a covered expatriate faces the IRC 877A mark-to-market exit tax on assets he or she is treated as owning (grantor-trust assets included, per the IRS expatriation rules; not verified in detail), and later distributions to US beneficiaries of covered gifts can be hit by IRC 2801. Moving the trust's trustee or control abroad makes it a foreign trust and can trigger tax on unrealised gains (IRC 684; not verified). Terminating or distributing the trust is not an estate-tax event once GST exemption covers it; distributed assets keep their carryover basis.

inheritance.summary: Assets given to the trust (up to the donors' USD 15 million exclusion each in 2026, USD 30 million for a couple) and all their later growth are outside the parents' taxable estates and, with GST exemption allocated, outside the children's and grandchildren's estates as well. Only assets kept outside the trust bear the 40% estate tax at death. Modelled as an estate-basis tax with a USD 30 million exemption: both parents fund the trust during life with their full exclusions; the remaining estate is taxed at 40%.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per donor for 2026 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32), indexed from 2027; GST exemption equals the basic exclusion (IRC 2631(c)). Annual exclusion gifts (USD 19,000 per donee) can also fund the trust, but need Crummey powers and do not carry GST exemption automatically.
inheritance.important_exceptions: The static figure understates the benefit and overstates the difference to direct holding in one respect. Understates: growth after funding escapes estate tax entirely (a USD 30 million trust growing at 5% a year is worth about USD 80 million after 20 years, all outside the estate), and the grantor's income-tax payments further shrink the taxable estate. Overstates: the standard regime in this file counts one USD 15 million exclusion, while a married couple can in principle shelter USD 30 million on death too through portability (with QDOT requirements when the surviving spouse is not a citizen). The cost: no basis step-up for trust assets (Rev. Rul. 2023-2), so up to 23.8% on embedded gains when the children sell. State estate or gift taxes are not reflected.

residency.tax_residency_test: Income tax: citizens always; non-citizens with a green card (lawful permanent residents) or meeting the substantial presence test (at least 31 days in the year and 183 days counting all current-year days, 1/3 of prior-year days and 1/6 of the second prior year), subject to the closer-connection exception. Estate tax: domicile. Leaving after holding a green card in 8 of the last 15 years (long-term resident) or renouncing citizenship triggers the IRC 877A exit tax for covered expatriates (net worth USD 2 million or more, average net income tax above USD 211,000 for 2026, or failure to certify compliance).

income.name: United States

income_tax.summary: US federal income tax only: 10% to 37% (2026 single brackets; standard deduction USD 16,100, modelled as the personal allowance). Austin, Texas adds no personal income tax: Texas has no state income tax and no local income tax was found for Austin. About 22% federal marginal rate at the 150,000 level. Employees pay 6.2% social security up to USD 184,500 plus 1.45% Medicare (plus 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on wages above USD 200,000, not modelled); the self-employed pay 15.3% (12.4% + 2.9%) on 92.35% of net earnings. Other states vary widely: nine have no wage income tax (for example Texas and Florida).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employment tax is 15.3% (12.4% social security + 2.9% Medicare) applied to 92.35% of net self-employment earnings (IRS Schedule SE line 4a/5b, opened 2026-10-15), so the rate on net earnings is 15.3% x 0.9235 = 14.13%. The 12.4% part stops at the wage base (USD 184,500 for 2026, i.e. net earnings of about USD 199,783 after the 92.35% factor); the cap field uses that point, but the 2.9% Medicare part is uncapped and a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax applies above USD 200,000 (single; IRS), neither modelled above the cap. Half of the SE tax is deductible in computing income tax (IRS), not modelled. Self-employed people may deduct the employer-equivalent half of self-employment tax (IRS, in adjusted gross income), so about 0.5 of their contributions reduce taxable income; the employee figure (0) governs the field.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Brackets are the 2026 US federal schedule for a single filer on TAXABLE income (IRS release), applied after the USD 16,100 standard deduction (field personal_allowance). Texas levies no state income tax (Texas Comptroller) and no Austin local income tax was found; the previous New York State and New York City layers were removed. Not modelled: the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on wages above USD 200,000 (employer withholding, single filer), the Net Investment Income Tax, itemised deductions, the QBI deduction, and FICA non-deductibility (social_security_deductible 0). Texas property tax and sales tax are not income taxes and are outside this field.

income.residence_routes: There is no digital nomad visa. EU and many other nationals can visit on ESTA or B-1/B-2 status but may not work for US clients while there, so a remote worker has no direct immigration route; long stays need a work visa (H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN for Canada/Mexico), an investor visa or family sponsorship, all employer- or relationship-based. US citizens need no immigration route but owe US tax on worldwide income wherever they live. A skilled employee at a US employer typically uses H-1B (annual lottery), L-1 intra-company transfer or O-1.

succession.name: United States
succession.summary: Federal law does not regulate inheritance; each state does. Almost every state lets you disinherit children, though a surviving spouse usually has a statutory elective share. Louisiana is the exception: it has forced heirship for children under 24 or disabled (Civil Code art. 1493). Trusts are widely available, the Hague Trusts Convention is signed but not in force, and family foundations exist mainly as US charities.
succession.family_claims: In most states a surviving spouse has an elective share or a community-property half (nine community-property states); children generally have no claim. Details differ by state. Exception: Louisiana only: forced heirs are children aged 23 or younger or permanently disabled; the forced portion is 25% of the estate with one forced heir and 50% with two or more (La. Civil Code art. 1493). Not read here.
succession.foreign_law_note: Succession conflict rules are state law: movables go by the law of the deceased's domicile, land by the law of its location. Some states let a testator choose the law of their domicile for a non-domiciliary estate (e.g. New York EPTL 3-5.1(h)); not verified here. Louisiana forced heirship also reaches property in Louisiana.
succession.trust_note: HCCH table: the United States signed on 13 June 1988 but has not ratified; the Convention is not in force. Domestic trusts are state law (the Uniform Trust Code and asset-protection trust statutes in some states). Foreign trusts are taxed under the grantor-trust rules and subject to Forms 3520 and 3520-A (not read here). Foundations: private foundations are tax-exempt charities (IRC sections 501(c)(3), 509, 4940 ff.); a non-charitable family foundation is not a standard vehicle.
open_questions: Elective share rules and the community-property states were stated from general knowledge; verify per state.
New York EPTL 3-5.1(h) and similar choice-of-law provisions were not read.
Whether any state (e.g. Wyoming) has a statutory non-charitable foundation law was not checked.
The federal estate tax and the 2026 exemption are out of scope.

immigration.name: United States
immigration.summary: US citizens need no permit. EU and other nationals can get a green card through EB-5 (USD 1,050,000, or USD 800,000 in a targeted employment area, 10 jobs) or live on a renewable E-2 treaty-investor visa if their country is on the treaty list. The Trump Gold Card (USD 1 million gift) is created by executive order and the USCIS form is posted, but filing is not open, so it is recorded as announced.
immigration.naturalisation: Five years as a lawful permanent resident (three if married to a US citizen), continuous residence and physical presence, English and civics tests (2025 test of 128 questions for N-400 filed from 20 October 2025).
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: The US does not require renunciation on naturalisation, but the applicant's own country may.

routes.name: US citizenship (no permit needed)
routes.summary: US citizens simply live in the United States; no visa, permit or investment is needed.
routes.requirements: Citizenship by birth in the US or to a US citizen parent, or by naturalisation. A US citizen has the right to enter, live and work in the US without any immigration status.
routes.tax_note: US citizens are taxed on worldwide income wherever they live.

sources.title: The Naturalization Interview and Test

routes.name: EB-5 immigrant investor (outside a targeted employment area)
routes.summary: A green card for investing USD 1,050,000 in a new commercial enterprise that creates at least 10 full-time US jobs. Residence is conditional for two years first.
routes.requirements: Investment of USD 1,050,000 (petitions filed on or after 15 March 2022) in a new commercial enterprise, directly or through a USCIS-designated regional center; at least 10 full-time qualifying jobs (35 hours a week). Amounts adjust for inflation (CPI-U) every 5 years from petitions filed on or after 1 January 2027. Regional Center Program visas are authorised through 30 September 2027. Conditional green card, then Form I-829 to remove conditions. Not available to US citizens.
routes.fees_note: USCIS returned several EB-5 filing fees to the pre-1 April 2024 amounts on 14 November 2025 (Form G-1055); the amounts were not read from the fee schedule. Visa-quota backlogs apply for some nationalities (Chinese, Indian).
routes.physical_presence: No minimum days; a conditional resident must keep the green card status (not abandon US residence)
routes.family: Spouse and unmarried children under 21 get green cards with the investor.
routes.tax_note: A green card makes the holder a US tax resident on worldwide income, and starts the clock for the exit tax after 8 of 15 years.

sources.title: About the EB-5 Visa Classification

routes.name: EB-5 immigrant investor (targeted employment area or infrastructure)
routes.summary: The same EB-5 green card at a reduced investment of USD 800,000 when the project is in a rural area or an area of high unemployment, or is an infrastructure project.
routes.requirements: Investment of USD 800,000 (petitions filed on or after 15 March 2022) in a targeted employment area (a rural area, or an area with unemployment at least 150% of the national average) or an infrastructure project; 10 full-time jobs; same conditional-residence process as standard EB-5. Regional Center Program visas are authorised through 30 September 2027. Not available to US citizens.
routes.physical_presence: No minimum days; a conditional resident must keep the green card status (not abandon US residence)
routes.family: Spouse and unmarried children under 21 get green cards with the investor.
routes.tax_note: A green card makes the holder a US tax resident on worldwide income.

sources.title: About the EB-5 Visa Classification

routes.name: E-2 treaty investor visa
routes.summary: A renewable non-immigrant visa for nationals of a treaty country who invest a substantial amount in a real US business that they direct. It does not lead to a green card.
routes.requirements: Must be a national of a treaty country; capital invested must be substantial, at risk and lawfully sourced; at least 50% ownership or operational control; the business must not be marginal. No fixed statutory minimum. Initial stay up to 2 years, renewable without limit while the business continues. EU states: the lists reviewed show Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Latvia and Lithuania as treaty countries and, by country notes, also the Netherlands, Spain, Slovakia and Slovenia; Cyprus, Hungary, Malta and Portugal were not listed; the sources disagree on Luxembourg, Poland, Romania and Sweden, so check the State Department list. Other nationals (UK, Canada, Japan and others) depend on the same list. US citizens do not need it.
routes.physical_presence: Live in the US to run the business; no day count
routes.family: Spouse and unmarried children under 21 can accompany; spouses may apply for work authorisation.
routes.tax_note: Substantial presence in the US makes the holder US tax resident.

routes.name: Trump Gold Card (USD 1 million gift)
routes.status_note: Created by Executive Order 14351 of 19 September 2025; USCIS posted Form I-140G but, as of the 9 October 2026 USCIS page, public filing is not open. Not enacted by Congress. Re-check before relying on it.
routes.summary: A proposed fast route to a green card (EB-1 or EB-2) in return for a USD 1 million gift to the US government. Created by executive order, not by law; USCIS has posted the form but filing is not open to the public.
routes.requirements: Executive Order 14351 (19 September 2025), not an Act of Congress. Per trumpcard.gov: gift of USD 1,000,000 per person including each family member, USD 15,000 non-refundable DHS fee per person, applicant must be admissible and have an available EB-1/EB-2 visa number (waits of a year or more for some countries). Registration is on trumpcard.gov; Form I-140G (edition 09/11/26) may be filed only through a USCIS online account after registration is confirmed, and USCIS 'will notify you' when filing opens. The USCIS page last updated 9 October 2026 says filing is not yet open. Corporate Gold Card (USD 2 million per employee) and Platinum Card (USD 5 million, not launched) are also announced. A legal challenge was reported in February 2026.
routes.physical_presence: No minimum days stated; holders become US tax residents
routes.family: Spouse and unmarried children under 21 can be included, each with a USD 1 million gift and USD 15,000 fee.
routes.tax_note: Holders are taxed on worldwide income (trumpcard.gov). The announced Platinum Card would allow up to 270 days a year in the US without US tax on non-US income; not launched.
